titleStmt.title: Separate visual pathways for perception and action
titleStmt.author: Goodale , Milner

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Separate visual pathways for perception and action

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: We propose that the ventral stream of projections from the striate cortex to the inferotemporal cortex plays the major role in the perceptual identification of objects, while the dorsal stream projecting from the striate cortex to the posterior parietal region mediates the required sensorimotor for visually guided transformations actions directed at such objects.

span.label: cortical visual pathways for perception and action
span.quote: Accumulating neuropsychological, electrophysiological and behavioural evidence suggests that the neural substrates of visual perception may be quite distinct from those underlying the visual control of actions.

span.label: review
span.quote: Despite the interactions between the dorsal and ventral systems, the converging lines of evidence reviewed above indicate that each stream uses visual information about objects and events in the world in different ways.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Different output requirements (perceptual identification vs online sensorimotor transformation) demand different visual computations, and this drives the anatomical segregation of the two streams.
span.quote: These differences are largely a reflection of the specific transformations of input required by perception and action.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Dorsal-stream processing proceeds without reaching consciousness, which keeps moment-to-moment viewer-centred information from disrupting the perceptual constancies computed in the ventral stream.
span.quote: It may be that information can be processed in the dorsal system without reaching consciousness, and that this prevents interference with the perceptual constancies intrinsic to many operations within the ventral system that do result in awareness.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Separate processing modules evolved because vision is put to functionally different uses.
span.quote: It seems plausible from a functional standpoint that separate processing modules would have evolved to mediate the different uses to which vision can be put.

span.label: The proposed division of labour between the two streams is not claimed to be absolute.
span.quote: We do not, however, wish to claim that the division of labour we are proposing is an absolute one.

span.label: Correlating human neuropsychological findings with monkey neurophysiology requires caution.
span.quote: While any correlations between human neuropsychology and monkey neurophysiology should only be made with caution, it is likely that humans share many features of visual processing with our primate relatives - particularly with the Old World monkeys in which most of the electrophysiology has been carried out.

span.label: The evidence base lacks detailed analyses of how task-specific most visuospatial disorders are.
span.quote: Unfortunately, we lack detailed analyses of the possible specificity of most such disorders: in many, the deficit may be restricted to particular behavioural tasks.

span.label: The paper replaces the principle by which the same two pathways are divided.
span.note: what this limits: any comparison between findings filed under the two accounts: the authors propose that the what-versus-how distinction, rather than the distinction between object vision and spatial vision, captures the functional dichotomy between the ventral and dorsal projections
span.quote: proposed that this distinction ('what' versus 'how') - rather than the distinction between object vision and spatial vision ('what' versus 'where') - captures more appropriately the functional dichotomy between the ventral and dorsal projections

span.label: An earlier term is criticised by name for grouping behaviours it could not separate.
span.note: what this limits: any use of the earlier localization account: the authors state that the notion of localization failed to distinguish between the many different patterns of behaviour that vary with the spatial location of visual stimuli, only some of which rely on tectal mechanisms
span.quote: However, the notion of 'localization' failed to distinguish between the many different patterns of behaviour that vary with the spatial location of visual stimuli, only some of which turn out to rely on tectal mechanisms

span.label: two control subjects put through the same manual matching task as the patient DF, over a series of randomly ordered trials
span.note: eliminates: the dissociation being a property of the task rather than of DF's lesion - the controls do the identical task, and the random order removes anticipation for everyone
span.quote: (A) In the manual matching task, DF and two control subjects were instructed to indicate the width of each plaque over a series of randomly ordered trials by separating the index finger and thumb of their right hand.

span.label: ventral stream
span.quote: We propose that the ventral stream of projections from the striate cortex to the inferotemporal cortex plays the major role in the perceptual identification of objects, while the dorsal stream projecting from the striate cortex to the posterior parietal region mediates the required sensorimotor for visually guided transformations actions directed at such objects.

span.label: dorsal stream
span.quote: We propose that the ventral stream of projections from the striate cortex to the inferotemporal cortex plays the major role in the perceptual identification of objects, while the dorsal stream projecting from the striate cortex to the posterior parietal region mediates the required sensorimotor for visually guided transformations actions directed at such objects.

span.label: localization
span.quote: However, the notion of 'localization' failed to distinguish between the many different patterns of behaviour that vary with the spatial location of visual stimuli, only some of which turn out to rely on tectal mechanisms

span.label: functional dichotomy
span.quote: proposed that this distinction ('what' versus 'how') - rather than the distinction between object vision and spatial vision ('what' versus 'where') - captures more appropriately the functional dichotomy between the ventral and dorsal projections

span.label: tectal mechanisms
span.quote: However, the notion of 'localization' failed to distinguish between the many different patterns of behaviour that vary with the spatial location of visual stimuli, only some of which turn out to rely on tectal mechanisms

span.label: the dorsal/ventral division - THE SAME ANATOMY, A NEW DIVIDING PRINCIPLE: the authors propose that what-versus-how, rather than the object-vision versus spatial-vision distinction, captures the functional dichotomy between the two projections; the fibre bundles are unchanged and the question used to sort them is not, so findings filed under the two accounts sort the same tissue differently
span.quote: proposed that this distinction ('what' versus 'how') - rather than the distinction between object vision and spatial vision ('what' versus 'where') - captures more appropriately the functional dichotomy between the ventral and dorsal projections

span.label: localization - A TERM THAT FAILED TO DISTINGUISH: the notion is said not to separate the many different patterns of behaviour that vary with the spatial location of a stimulus, only some of which rely on tectal mechanisms, so one word covered several mechanisms and the paper says so
span.quote: However, the notion of 'localization' failed to distinguish between the many different patterns of behaviour that vary with the spatial location of visual stimuli, only some of which turn out to rely on tectal mechanisms

span.label: the ventral stream - DEFINED BY WHAT IT IS FOR, NOT BY WHERE IT GOES: proposed to play the major role in the perceptual identification of objects, in the sentence that also names the dorsal stream as the other half of the proposal; the stream is identified here by a function rather than by its anatomical destination
span.quote: We propose that the ventral stream of projections from the striate cortex to the inferotemporal cortex plays the major role in the perceptual identification of objects, while the dorsal stream projecting from the striate cortex to the posterior parietal region mediates the required sensorimotor for visually guided transformations actions directed at such objects.

span.label: extends → Ungerleider and Mishkin's (1982) two-visual-systems model ('what' versus 'where')
span.quote: In this article, it is proposed that this distinction ('what' versus 'how') - rather than the distinction between object vision and spatial vision ('what' versus 'where') - captures more appropriately the functional dichotomy between the ventral and dorsal projections.

span.label: ventral stream —contrasted-with→ dorsal stream
span.quote: We propose that the ventral stream of projections from the striate cortex to the inferotemporal cortex plays the major role in the perceptual identification of objects, while the dorsal stream projecting from the striate cortex to the posterior parietal region mediates the required sensorimotor for visually guided transformations actions directed at such objects.

span.label: mean
span.quote: In interpreting all these graphs, it is the slope of the function that is important rather than the absolute values plotted, since the placement of the IREDs and the size of the hand and fingers varied somewhat from subject to subject. Bars represent means +__ SE.

span.label: standard error
span.quote: In interpreting all these graphs, it is the slope of the function that is important rather than the absolute values plotted, since the placement of the IREDs and the size of the hand and fingers varied somewhat from subject to subject. Bars represent means +__ SE.

span.label: The visual-form agnosic patient DF scaled her grip aperture to object width normally when reaching to grasp, despite being unable to perceive that width.
span.quote: However, when she was asked simply to reach out and pick up the block, the aperture between her index finger and thumb changed systematically with the width of the object, just as in normal subjects (Fig. 2B).

span.label: The same patient's manual estimates of object width bore no relation to actual object size and were highly variable trial to trial.
span.quote: When she was asked to indicate the width of a single block by means of her index finger and thumb, her matches bore no relationship to the dimensions of the object and showed considerable trial to trial variability (Fig. 2A).

span.label: The dorsal/ventral division cannot be reduced to the magnocellular/parvocellular retinal division, because both streams receive input from both pathways.
span.quote: In short, it now appears that the dorsal and the ventral streams each receive inputs from both the magno and the parvo pathways.

span.label: Spatial attention is not the exclusive property of the dorsal stream; attentional modulation occurs in ventral-stream areas as well.
span.quote: We conclude that spatial attention is physiologically non-unitary 55, and may be as much associated with the ventral system as with the dorsal.

span.label: The authors conclude that cortical visual modularity is organised by output requirements all the way from input to motor output, not only by input categories.
span.quote: Functional modularity in cortical visual systems, we believe, extends from input right through to output.

span.label: Parietal damage produces a broad visuomotor disorder (grasp shaping and hand orientation), not merely a disorder of spatial localization.
span.quote: Despite her profound inability to recognize the size, shape and orientation of visual objects, DF showed strikingly accurate guidance of hand and finger movements directed at the very same objects

span.term: ventral stream vs dorsal stream (perception vs visuomotor control)
span.quote: We propose that the ventral stream of projections from the striate cortex to the inferotemporal cortex plays the major role in the perceptual identification of objects, while the dorsal stream projecting from the striate cortex to the posterior parietal region mediates the required sensorimotor for visually guided transformations actions directed at such objects.

span.label: 'what' versus 'how' (as opposed to 'what' versus 'where')
span.quote: proposed that this distinction ('what' versus 'how') - rather than the distinction between object vision and spatial vision ('what' versus 'where') - captures more appropriately the functional dichotomy between the ventral and dorsal projections.

span.label: viewer-centred coding of shape
span.quote: For this purpose, coding of shape would need to be largely 'viewer-centred '49, with the egocentric coordinates of the surface of the object or its contours being computed each time the action occurs.

span.label: width of the target plaque/block
span.quote: (A) In the manual matching task, DF and two control subjects were instructed to indicate the width of each plaque over a series of randomly ordered trials by separating the index finger and thumb of their right hand.

span.quote: However, when she was asked simply to reach out and pick up the block, the aperture between her index finger and thumb changed systematically with the width of the object, just as in normal subjects (Fig. 2B).

span.label: control subjects (CG and CJ) versus patient DF
span.term: control subjects (CG and CJ) versus patient DF
span.quote: In DF, unlike the controls (CG and CJ), the aperture between the finger and thumb was not systematically related to the width of the target.

span.label: approximately 45 cm — viewing distance at which the plaques were presented in the matching and grasping tasks
span.quote: In both (A) the manual matching task and (B) the grasping task, five white plaques (each with an overall area of 25 c m 2 o n the top surface, but with dimensions ranging from 5 x 5 cm to 2.5 x 10 cm) were presented, one at a time, at a viewing distance of approximately 45 cm.

span.label: 5 x 5 cm to 2.5 x 10 cm — range of plaque dimensions used as the stimulus set (all of equal top-surface area)
span.quote: In both (A) the manual matching task and (B) the grasping task, five white plaques (each with an overall area of 25 c m 2 o n the top surface, but with dimensions ranging from 5 x 5 cm to 2.5 x 10 cm) were presented, one at a time, at a viewing distance of approximately 45 cm.
